title: fix: resolve incorrect Rayleigh MGF values via erfcx formulation
body:
Resolves #15456.

## Description

This pull request:

-   Fixes the Rayleigh MGF, which misplaced a parenthesis so that `mgf(0, sigma)` returned `sqrt(pi/2)` instead of `1`.
-   Evaluates the corrected formula via `erfcx(-sigma*t/sqrt(2))`, which additionally avoids overflow and catastrophic cancellation for negative `t` (the naive regrouping returns `1` at `σt = -10` and `NaN` at `σt = -40`).
-   Applies the same fix to the C implementation and swaps `exp`/`erf` dependencies for `erfcx` in `manifest.json`.
-   Updates all documentation examples, the `ctor` docs, and the namespace type declarations.
-   Adds scipy-generated test fixtures with negative-`t` coverage and rewrites `test.mgf.js` against them.

## Related Issues

This pull request has the following related issues:

-   #15456

## Questions

No. One note for reviewers: a single small-scale fixture point sits at 54 ULP against a 100 ULP tolerance (both sides within ~1e-14 of truth; fixture quadrature noise). The C implementation mirrors the reviewed spec but was not compiled locally — CI build will confirm.

## Other

The fixture generator is `test/fixtures/python/runner.py` (per the reviewer's gist); fixtures were generated with scipy 1.18.1. Verified locally: 3000/3000 fixture assertions pass, `mgf(0, sigma) === 1`, and the negative-`t` regression points behave (`mgf(-10, 1)` ≈ 0.0097, finite at `mgf(-40, 1)`).

#### Disclosure

I used an AI assistant to help trace the `dists` implementations and to numerically cross-check the Rayleigh MGF against its closed form and the MGF definition integral. I independently confirmed the diagnosis by executing the code locally, and I verified every corrected value the same way before updating the docs. The `erfcx` formulation itself follows the reviewer's specification.
